subject: LLM inference MAP — weekly scorecard & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: LLM inference MAP — weekly scorecard & next steps

Team — attaching this week's MAP scorecard and a short readout. Key takeaways up front, then owners and actions.

Attachments: scorecard_q3w28.csv (csv) — summary sheet; latency_traces_wk28.zip (zip) — raw traces and flamegraphs

Executive summary (MAP milestone: perf sign-off for phase-2 canary):
- OptiHealth benchmark window (production-ish traffic replay): 2026-07-13 -> 2026-07-19
- Observed models (serving config noted in scorecard): Llama-2-Chat-70B-Q4, Red-Regional-13B, Red-Lite-7B
- P50 / P95 / P99 latency (end-to-end, client-observed)
  - Llama-2-Chat-70B-Q4 (q4f16): p50 42 ms, p95 182 ms, p99 312 ms — throughput 240 tokens/s (replica, batch=8)
  - Red-Regional-13B (int8): p50 30 ms, p95 120 ms, p99 210 ms — throughput 390 tokens/s
  - Red-Lite-7B (fp16): p50 18 ms, p95 68 ms, p99 120 ms — throughput 850 tokens/s
- Errors: transient 502 spikes during 2 short intervals (replay bursts); not correlated with model swaps. See latency_traces_wk28.zip
- Cost: unit token cost roughly inline with SLO targets; batching gains significant at tail of hour spikes.

Decisions needed before canary (owners):
1) Kernel / compilation verification for Llama-2-Chat-70B-Q4 (Marcus) — reproduce p99 tail with raw kernel traces; confirm optimized kernel is in use.
2) Batching policy tweak (Tessa) — propose increasing max_batch_size to 12 during low-concurrency windows and fall back aggressively on cross-request timeout 20ms; test in staging.
3) Canary config and rollback window (Monica) — define 48-hour canary window + automatic fallback triggers for p95 > 220ms or error rate > 1.5%.
4) Customer communication / schedule (me) — confirm OptiHealth test start + visibility dashboard link.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Marcus: upload raw kernel traces and short runbook for reproducing p99 spike (due 2026-07-21 EOD). [Attachment: latency_traces_wk28.zip]
- Tessa: create canary-config-v2.yaml with batch policy and autoscale guardrails, push to staging, and run 3 stress passes (due 2026-07-22 AM). [Related: gist link below]
- Monica: draft canary rollout timeline and Ops rotation (due 2026-07-21 noon).
- Soojin: confirm OptiHealth schedule + send invite for decision sync (meeting scheduled in thread).

Notes / quick observations inside the scorecard:
- The largest source of p99 variance is KV cache warmup; we see consistent reductions after a 300-request warm window.
- Cross-request batching reduces cost by ~18% on average but needs careful latency SLO tuning for OptiHealth's interactive flows.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AaB-Scorecard (scorecard), https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9843

Prioritizing owners above — reply if you disagree or need a different due date.

Thanks,
— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick ask: can you push the kernel traces to the shared run artifacts bucket and include the exact commit hash for the runtime image used in the replay? I want to correlate the p99 with kernel selection logs. If it's easier, point me to the exact file in latency_traces_wk28.zip.

On the canary guards, the p95 threshold looks fine; I want an explicit telemetry flag to disable the adaptive batching in case the initial canary has higher tail variance.

Marcus

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM inference MAP — weekly scorecard & next steps

Adding proposed changes and small config snippet below. I ran two staging passes overnight with the new batching policy; tail improved ~12% on p99 for batch-friendly traces.

Proposed canary-config-v2.yaml (excerpt):
  max_batch_size: 12
  batch_timeout_ms: 8
  cross_request_timeout_ms: 20
  adaptive_batching: true
  adaptive_backoff_threshold_ms: 150
  kill_switch_flag: telemetry.adaptive_batching_disable

I pushed the snippet here: https://gist.github.com/tessa/batching-snippet
Next steps I will take:
- Push full canary-config-v2.yaml to staging and run 3 stress passes (today).
- If Marcus can confirm kernel traces by EOD, I'll include a fallback plan to force max_batch_size=8 during the first 6 hours of canary.

On the KV cache warmup: I have a quick patch to pre-warm popular prefixes; will test in pre-prod today and report results tomorrow.

Tessa
Production Performance Manager
[Related: https://gist.github.com/tessa/batching-snippet]

Thanks, Soojin — this readout is helpful. OptiHealth is aligned to start the canary on Monday 2026-07-27. A couple questions: 
- Do you recommend the 48-hour window as final? We prefer a shorter initial window if safe (24h) with the option to extend if we see slow tail issues.
- For rollback triggers, can we add a synthetic traffic check in addition to p95/p99 thresholds? We'd like an automated heartbeat test every 30 minutes during canary to validate end-to-end correctness and latency.

If you can confirm the times and the telemetry flag for adaptive batching, we'll allocate OptiHealth engineering on-call.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Head of ML Ops, OptiHealth

Appreciate the quick replies — summary and final asks below so we can close pre-canary tasks: 
- Canary start: 2026-07-27 09:00 PT (OptiHealth confirmed)
- Canary window: 24h initial + auto-extend to 48h if any synthetic heartbeat failures or p95 > 220ms for two consecutive 30-minute windows. Monica, please prepare the Ops rotation for the initial 24h (due 2026-07-21 noon was requested; if delayed please flag).
- Marcus: please upload kernel traces (path + runtime commit hash) to the artifacts bucket and reply in-thread when done.
- Tessa: finalize and push canary-config-v2.yaml to staging, run 3 stress passes, and include the kill_switch_flag in the deployment manifest. Link to gist is fine for review.
- Me: will send the OptiHealth invite and link to the shared dashboard (Drive scorecard + Kibana canary dashboard).

Meeting: Decision sync — Tue 2026-07-27 08:30 PT (30m) to review first-hour telemetry and confirm fallback. Invite to follow.

Closing notes: We are green to proceed once the above artifacts are in place. Thanks everyone for the tight turnaround.
